question: The electric flux through the region between the plates of a capacitor varies with time as $\Phi_E = 1.5 \times 10^6 t^2$, where $\Phi_E$ is in $\text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-1}$ and $t$ is in second. Determine the displacement current at $t = 2.0\text{ s}$. Explain whether the displacement current remains constant with time.

options.A:
$I_D=\varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$.
For $\Phi_E=1.5\times10^6t^2$, $\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}=3.0\times10^6t$. At $t=2.0\text{ s}$, $\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}=6.0\times10^6\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$.
$I_D=(8.85\times10^{-12})(6.0\times10^6)=5.31\times10^{-5}\text{ A}$. Since $I_D\propto t$, it is not constant.
options.B: $I_D=\varepsilon_0\Phi_E$. At $t=2.0\text{ s}$, $I_D=5.31\times10^{-5}\text{ A}$ and remains constant because $\varepsilon_0$ is constant.
options.C: $\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}=1.5\times10^6t$. At $t=2.0\text{ s}$, $I_D=2.66\times10^{-5}\text{ A}$ and decreases with time.
options.D: $I_D=\dfrac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$. At $t=2.0\text{ s}$, $I_D=6.78\times10^{17}\text{ A}$ and is constant.
